info.name: Pharma Aggregator Server API
info.description:
Complete Postman Collection for the Pharma Aggregator Server (Spring Boot 3, Java 21).

**Base path:** all requests are relative to `{{baseUrl}}` which should include the application context path `/api/v1` (e.g. `http://localhost:8080/api/v1`).

**Authentication:** The API uses a two-step OTP login flow that issues a stateless JWT:
1. `POST /authentication/login` — validate username/password, triggers an OTP email.
2. `POST /authentication/verify-otp` — validate the OTP and receive `accessToken` + `refreshToken`.

The **Verify OTP & Get Token** request automatically stores the returned tokens into the `access_token` / `refresh_token` collection variables via a test script. All secured requests in this collection use Bearer Auth referencing `{{access_token}}` automatically — just run the Authentication folder first.

Use `POST /authentication/refresh` to rotate an expired access token using the stored refresh token.

**Note on current security posture:** at the time this collection was generated, `SecurityConfig` permits all requests (`anyRequest().permitAll()`) while the JWT filter chain is fully wired up. Endpoints that read the authenticated principal via `Authentication`/`UserDetailsImpl` (e.g. most of the Products and Seller Profile folders) still require a valid Bearer token to resolve the current user, even though Spring Security itself won't reject an anonymous request at the gate. Endpoints that don't read the principal work with or without a token.

item.name: Authentication

request.description: STEP 1: Validates username + password, and sends an OTP to the seller's registered email. On success, returns username to be used in the verify-otp step. Public endpoint.

STEP 2: Validates the 6-digit OTP sent to email and issues a JWT access token + refresh token. Automatically saves 'access_token' and 'refresh_token' to collection variables for use in subsequent authenticated requests. Public endpoint.

exec: pm.test('Access token received and saved', function () {

request.description: Exchanges a valid refresh token for a new access token (and rotated refresh token). Automatically updates 'access_token' and 'refresh_token' collection variables. Public endpoint.
Revokes the supplied refresh token server-side. Client should also discard the stored access token (JWT is stateless).

Resets a user's password by validating their current password first. Requires username, currentPassword, and a newPassword meeting complexity rules (min 8 chars, 1 digit, 1 lowercase, 1 uppercase, 1 special character, no whitespace).
Sends a password-reset OTP to the user's registered email address.
Verifies the OTP sent via forgot-password and returns a short-lived reset token used to authorize the actual password reset. Automatically saves 'reset_token' collection variable.

exec: pm.test('Reset token received and saved', function () {

request.description: Validates whether a password-reset token is still valid (not expired/used) before allowing the user to submit a new password.
Sets a new password using the reset token obtained from the forgot-password / verify-otp flow (instead of the current password). New password must meet complexity rules.

item.description: Two-step OTP login (login -> verify-otp) issuing JWT access/refresh tokens, plus password reset flows. The verify-otp and refresh requests auto-save tokens to collection variables consumed by {{access_token}} across the rest of the collection.

request.description: Adds stock for a product. If batchLotNumber already exists for this product, tops up that batch's stockQuantity (rejects with 400 if the supplied expiryDate doesn't match what's on file); otherwise creates a brand-new batch. Writes one STOCK_IN StockLedger row and returns it. Requires the authenticated seller to own the product (401 otherwise).

request.description: Debits stock for a product using FIFO (oldest manufacturingDate batch first), spanning multiple batches if one isn't enough to cover the requested quantity. Returns one StockLedger row per batch touched, all sharing the same referenceId so they can be traced back to one order. Returns 409 Conflict if the requested quantity exceeds total available stock across all batches.
